title: Kernel-ranking entropy spike: alerting, fast-quarantine, and mitigation experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a capacity wave on 2026-02-08 we observed several short-lived spikes in kernel-ranking entropy which correlated with p95/p99 latency regressions for multi-tenant inference pools. This ticket captures follow-ups: an automated early-warning signal, a lightweight quarantine mechanism to route affected microbatches off the suspect kernel set, and a small suite of experiments to reduce probe amplification risk. Goal: detect entropy spikes within 30s and mitigate latency impact within 90s without broad capacity churn.
acceptance_criteria: Alert fires within 30s of sustained kernel-ranking entropy increase > 3x baseline for a 60s window
Quarantine rule can be toggled via feature flag to redirect new microbatches away from top-3 suspect kernels for at least two minutes
Runbook documented with play-by-play and validated in canary cluster (canary run demonstrates >50% p95 reduction when quarantine applied)
Two mitigation experiments completed with clear success/failure criteria and next-step recommendations
action_items: (A) Implement entropy metric: normalized kernel-rank-entropy per worker and emit to telemetry (ENG: Lars + Priya) - owner: Lars
(B) Build Alert: composite alert combining entropy + microbatch p95 trend; add PagerDuty policy (ENG: SRE) - owner: Miguel
(C) Fast-quarantine feature: config-driven route exclusion for suspect kernels; default to dry-run (ENG: runtime) - owner: Priya
(D) Experiment 1: decrease probe rate from 1 probe/10s -> 1 probe/30s for mixed-quant models (runtime flag) - owner: Matthew
(E) Experiment 2: introduce small randomized backoff in kernel candidate scoring update loop - owner: Anika
(F) Update console dashboard with per-kernel entropy and quarantine status; link in runbook - owner: UX/Console
mitigation_playbook: 1) When alert fires, enable quarantine dry-run and observe impact for 2m. 2) If p95 improves >20%, promote quarantine and notify routing service. 3) Rollback if overall throughput drops >10% or error rate increases. 4) Open post-run notes and schedule follow-up retro.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive quarantine reduces tail latency quickly but can mask underlying capacity problems if relied on long-term.
We decided quarantine will be a short-lived mitigation (default 2 minutes) and must be accompanied by capacity evaluation and kernel curation.
Telemetry needs: add per-tenant entropy breakdown to understand customer exposure; prioritized after initial rollout.
If quarantine causes throughput regression, next step is automated canary rollback and scheduler backoff tuning.
Cross-team reviewers requested: SRE, Runtime, Console, and Solutions Engineering for customer communication templates.
